It is for people and by people, and it cannot be replicated. With TBA, we will show up to experience the moment, the tension, the beauty. And at a time when we can get lost in technology, critical global issues, and the mess of the day-to-day, taking a moment for you—for art—is a radical act. This September, for just five days, join us. Sit with artists as they generously and fearlessly present their work. Share a communal movement. Experience the art of our time. events.summary: The memoirella is a great form of literature that fits somewhere between an essay and a memoir. The term was coined by Banana Pitch Press’s Founding Editor, Michelle Kicherer, who is here to teach her first-ever memoirella class. In this class we will read a few novellas to borrow from their medium-length structures, as well as several essays and memoirs. We’ll pick these works apart on a craft level, asking what these works did to make them successful, then apply those tools to your work. The first few weeks of the class will be focused on generative writing for your memoirella, and throughout the cohort we will have different types of workshops: one focused on opening pages; one on back-of-the-book summaries and 1-page pitches; and chapter excerpts. We will conclude the course with some talks around publishing. This class is meant to be as helpful as possible, but also fun! We’ll learn from each other and foster a positive and productive classroom environment. Course Takeaways ● How to start a memoirella with a hook and purpose ● What other novellas, essays and memoirs set up for and what those stories deliver ● How to structure your memoirella ● How and when to shrink it down to an essay, or expand it into a full-length memoir Materials Please bring a notebook and writing utensil to each class for brief in-class writing activities. I highly encourage pen and papering for the exercises we’ll be doing. A Note on Workshops Workshops are not mandatory, but are a wonderful way to receive feedback on your work. Each writer will have several opportunities to submit their work for review and written feedback. Please do plan on reading and providing feedback on your peers’ work so we can all support each other equally. Reading List Includes work from Stephanie Foo, Rachel Kushner, Susan Kiyoto Ito, Ta-Nehisi Coates, Chloé Cooper Jones, Karl Ove Knausgaard, and others
events.title: 3 Month Short Memoir Intensive: writing the memoirella

events.summary: This course for dedicated writers is designed to guide you through the writing and/or revising of your novel. It runs from September through May. You’ll read excerpts from published novels by authors including Han Kang, Tommy Orange, Lina Meruane, Mitchell S. Jackson, Deborah Levy, and Susan Steinberg, as well as craft essays by authors including Dorothy Allison, Jane Alison, and Alexander Chee. Some weeks you’ll have craft assignments to complete outside of class, and other weeks we’ll do in-class exercises together. After the first month of meetings, two students will workshop each week. Each student will have the opportunity to workshop five times, turning in up to 25 double-spaced pages per submission. Students should be prepared to read and comment on up to 50 pages of their classmates’ work each week, in addition to keeping up with their own writing. Download the syllabus for Nine-month online novel intensive here. Please note: this writing class is designed for adults 18 years and older. Access Program We want our writing classes and Delves to be accessible to everyone, regardless of income and background. We understand that our tuition structure can present obstacles for some people. Our Access Program offers writing class and Delve tuitions at a reduced rate. Most writing classes have at least one access spot available. Please apply here for access rate tuition. Contact Susan Moore at susan@literary-arts.org if you have questions. Refund policy: If you need to cancel your registration for the 9-month novel class, the following refund schedule applies: If you cancel at least 5 business days or more before a class begins, you will receive a credit to use on a future class, minus 15% of the tuition. Or you can request a refund of the tuition, minus 25% of the tuition. 4 business days until 24 hours or less before a class begins, you will receive a credit minus 20% of the tuition. No refunds are given 4 business days or less before a class begins. 24 hours or less before a class begins, no refund or credits will be given. “Cari Luna is one of the most incredible educators I’ve ever had. events.summary: Hailed by American Songwriter as "one of America's most intriguing, creative, and idiosyncratic voices," Eilen Jewell rises from the ashes on her captivating new album, Get Behind The Wheel, picking up the pieces of her shattered world and finding new purpose and meaning after watching her marriage, her band, and what felt like her entire career fall apart in a series of spectacular, heartbreaking implosions. Co-produced by multi-instrumental wizard Will Kimbrough \(with Todd Snider and Hayes Carll\), the collection pushes the acclaimed singer and songwriter's trademark blend of vintage roots-noir into more psychedelic territory, with spacious, cinematic arrangements complementing her revelatory explorations of grief, loss, resilience, and redemption. An Idaho native, Jewell built her career the old fashioned way, touring relentlessly with the kind of undeniable live show that converts the uninitiated into instant acolytes. Over the course of nine albums, she's crisscrossed the globe countless times and shared bills with the likes of Lucinda Williams, Loretta Lynn, Mavis Staples, Wanda Jackson, George Jones, and Emmylou Harris. Rolling Stone lauded Jewell's "clever writing," while NPR declared that she has a "sweet and clear voice with a killer instinct lurking beneath the shiny surface," and The Washington Post mused that "if Neko Case, Madeleine Peyroux and Billie Holiday had a baby girl who grew up to front a rockabilly band, she'd probably sound a lot like Eilen Jewell." events.summary: Reduce your social anxiety. Increase your confidence. Learn to navigate the world. Begin changing your psychology. Our newest class series isn't therapy, but it is incredibly therapeutic. We'll leverage the power of applied \(or process\) improvisation to bring the tools of improv to our daily lives. We'll anchor much of our work in the teachings & approaches of Augusto Boal and Paulo Friere, two educators who helped bring this style of improvisation to the world. Together, we'll learn how to: 🗣️ Share our most powerful life stories with honesty & vulnerability 💥 Explore those stories with creativity & support 👁️ See & experience our lives through the lens of others 💪🏼 Discover our psychological strengths and, most importantly... ❤️ Evolve our relationships through the power of insight 🗣️ 1:1 Sessions Included The practice of applied improvisation is fun, but also requires vulnerability. For this reason, this series includes a 30-60min 1:1 session with your teacher. In these virtual sessions, we'll discuss and celebrate your breakthroughs and then examine the patterns that have emerged from your work that might be holding you back from even deeper successes.
events.title: Improv for Personal Development | Support for anxiety & depression

This Event is 21\+ ---------------------------------------- Left on Tenth: Left on Tenth is a hard-hitting, horn-driven rock group based out of Portland, OR. Their catalog incorporates many varieties of music that span from ska and reggae to latin, punk, and funk. The seductive booming brass section paired with tight, dancy rhythm section produce an optimal live performance that captivates audiences and keeps them engaged for their entire set. Having spent their formative days in the dimly-lit basement bars of Bozeman, MT the group has been known to consistently play out 150\+ shows a year. Small tours across the western states have attracted audiences that expanded their range of capabilities. The band has shared the stage for acts including The Wailers, Karl Denson’s Tiny Universe, Stone Foxes, Naked Giants, MarchFourth, Polyrhythmics, along with others. Their most recent release "Croak” was engineered and produced by Zach Bloomstein \(Portugal The Man, Glitterfox\). BendreTheGiant: From Portland, Oregon, BendreTheGiant is a neo-soul/power-pop group led by Ben Estrada. Estrada has been releasing music since 2020, but his 2024 releases mark the first time he has brought in outside collaborators: BendreTheGiant is now a six-piece band that includes keyboardist Delos Erickson, guitarist Avery Scanlon, bassist Eli Hansen, drummer Nate Hansen, and saxophonist Ben Harris. events.summary: Surgery always carries some level of risk, and not every unexpected outcome is the result of negligence. However, when a healthcare professional fails to meet the accepted standard of medical care and that failure causes avoidable harm, the situation may amount to Surgical Negligence. Determining the difference often requires a careful review of medical records, expert opinions, and the circumstances surrounding the procedure. Warning signs can include operating on the wrong site, delayed treatment of complications, retained surgical instruments, anesthesia errors, or inadequate post-operative care. It is also important to consider whether the patient was properly informed of the risks before consenting to surgery. Establishing negligence involves proving that the injury was preventable and directly caused by substandard care rather than an unavoidable complication. Because these cases can be medically and legally complex, professional legal guidance is essential. Ciano Carroll Solicitors represents individuals who believe they have suffered avoidable harm due to medical errors and helps them understand whether they may have a valid claim. Their experience in handling complex medical negligence matters enables clients to navigate the legal process with confidence. By working with independent medical experts and thoroughly investigating each case, the firm evaluates whether the required legal standard for negligence has been met. Anyone concerned about the outcome of a surgical procedure should seek advice as early as possible to protect their legal rights. Understanding the distinction between an accepted surgical risk and Surgical Negligence is the first step toward determining whether compensation may be available.
events.title: How can you tell if a surgical complication was actually negligence?

events.summary: The Multnomah Arts Center (MAC) in Portland, Oregon will open two new exhibitions in its Front and Center Galleries this August. tende·r·eprisal // futu·re·prise, a group exhibition of bronze works created by multiple artists through a collaborative process led by elijah jamal asani, will be featured in the Front Gallery. In the Center Gallery, large-scale wood sculptures by Philip A. Robinson Jr. will be paired with functional and sculptural ceramic works by Swapna Mukhopadhyay. Both exhibitions run August 7–September 12, 2026, with a joint reception on Thursday, August 20, from 6 to 8 p.m. elijah jamal asani, a Nigerian-American artist, convened an intergenerational group of regional Black artists to create a collection of contemporary bronze artifacts. Their work was made in response to the historic theft of the Benin Bronzes. “Dating back to the 13th century, artists from the Kingdom of Benin, which is in modern-day southern Nigeria, cast bronze into sacred altar pieces and vessels of ancestral memory,” says asani. “However, in 1897, thousands of these bronze artifacts were looted by British forces.” They have yet to be repatriated. As an act of “selfdetermined restitution,” asani worked with other Black artists to create new bronzes. MAC is honored to exhibit eleven of these sculptures, created by Adriene Cruz, Midnite Seed Abioto, Intisar Abioto, Hanifah Abioto, Vaughn Kimmons, Turiya Raiah, Nyasiah Calixte, Lea Dry, Hannah Dry, Nawens Dry, and elijah jamal asani. Swapna Mukhopadhyay creates functional and sculptural porcelain works, all hand built. “The combination of aesthetics and functionality in handmade folk artifacts has always fascinated me,” she says. “My grandmother made traditional Bengali quilts (kanthas) and wove mats for sitting on the floor (asanas). I now realize how deeply I was influenced by watching her work.” Delicate drawn elements adorn many of her ceramic surfaces, and several recent works incorporate textiles and found objects. Mukhopadhyay describes her process as “improvising around what’s available,” informed by her longtime study of ethnomathematics. A retired PSU professor, she sees mathematics as inherent to creative practice and creative expression as integral to daily life across many cultures. Her ceramic pieces are often small in scale and characterized by what she calls their “putting togetherness.” Philip A. Robinson Jr. is a sculptor and conceptual artist whose work has been exhibited nationally and internationally. Working primarily in wood and metal, Robinson creates large-scale figurative and patterned works that explore memory, structure, and identity. “My practice examines structure as a living system—how materials carry memory, how patterns encode history, and how built environments shape identity,” he explains. “Whether in wood or steel, I am asking how structure holds memory—and how we locate ourselves within it.” The exhibition will include pieces from several bodies of work, including a 42” x 61” sculpture from Welcome In, which examines belonging, and several works from The House of Regina, which honor the legacy of his late mother, Dr. Regina Arnold. Robinson holds a BFA in Studio Art from Skidmore College and an MFA in Sculpture from the Mason Gross School of the Arts at Rutgers University. The Multnomah Arts Center is located at 7688 SW Capitol Hwy, Portland, OR, 97219. It is open Monday – Thursday 9 a.m. to 9:30 p.m., and Friday – Saturday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The galleries are free and open to the public during these hours. Additional Information: The Multnomah Arts Center is a part of Portland Parks & Recreation. MAC offers programs in a wide range of visual, music, movement, theater, and literary arts at an affordable cost to people of all ages. In addition to this vibrant arts education program, MAC runs a community-based visual arts exhibition program, which includes the MAC Front & Center Galleries. MAC also hosts theatre, music and dance performances, and other special events. The Multnomah Arts Center Association (MACA) is an all-volunteer, 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that exists to support equity and access to arts education at MAC. MACA provides scholarships, supports community engagements efforts, and provides specialized arts equipment and facility improvements. Their efforts expand opportunities and enhance the experience of students, instructors, and the community at-large. For more information about MAC or MACA, please call 503.823.2787 or visit www.multnomahartscenter.org

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Last Thursday Artist Reception August 27, 6 to 9pm. Show Dates: August 27 through September 21. Outside City Limits Forget the commute. Turn the car around! Leave civilization behind and delight in the fused-glass landscapes of Linda Gerrard and wander through the threaded tree paintings of Michelle L. Purvis instead. Michelle’s lifelong fascination with trees, mountains, and how they relate to humans strongly influences her art. In this series of framed acrylic paintings on paper, each work is a portrait of a specific tree, dressed in embroidered finery to fit its personality. She made their acquaintance and sketched them from life while she was camping or on vacation. While they may have been created completely in her studio, Linda’s fused-glass landscapes evoke a real sense of natural place. Starting with a base sheet of glass, she builds her images by arranging and kiln-firing layer after layer of colored glass, often leaving lovely textured details on the surface. Linda and Michelle, two long-time members of the gallery, invite you to take in the vistas of meadow, marsh and mountainside, to reach out to stroke the colorful bark of the trees or a heron’s plumage, and to discover what lies just Outside City Limits. events.summary: Join Wen Wu School Portland for weekly Wild Goose Qigong practice, including tai chi warm-ups, acupressure self-massage, and walking meditation. 11 AM – Noon |Fridays, May 1 – October 30, 2026 Join Wen Wu School Portland in exploring Dayan, or Wild Goose Qigong, an ancient Chinese movement art developed to promote health, well-being, and longevity. Drop-in participation welcome! Wild Goose \(“Dayan” 大雁 in Chinese\) Qigong is an ancient Chinese Taoist movement art that nurtures one’s inner energy – Qi – and restores a healthy mind and body. The 64 movement first set mimics the wild goose, a highly revered animal of ancient China. With regular practice one can learn to access Qi for self-healing, restore vital energy, and strengthen one’s immune system to promote a healthy, balanced, and long life. Join Wen Wu School Portland for weekly Wild Goose Qigong practice classes, which include tai chi warm-ups, acupressure self-massage, and walking meditation through the Garden. events.summary: Liz Phair Throughout her career, Liz Phair has continued to defy expectations and break barriers. She has released five albums, sold over five million records, composed music for television, and received two GRAMMY nominations. In 2019, she published a memoir, Horror Stories \(Random House\), which the LA Times called "a raw look at fame, motherhood and aging with all the unbridled honesty of the songs that put the singer in the spotlight in the first place." In 2023, Phair toured to celebrate the 30th anniversary of her widely-loved debut, Exile in Guyville, performing the record in its entirety at sold-out shows across the US. An 18-track double album loosely framed as a song-by-song reply to The Rolling Stones' Exile on Main St., Exile In Guyville was dubbed a classic upon arrival. It is now regarded as a feminist landmark, recently cracking the top ten of Pitchfork's "Best 150 Albums of the 1990s" \(\#4\) and the top 100 of Rolling Stone's "Best 500 Albums of All Time" \(\#56\). Sleater-Kinney Now three decades into their partnership and no less ferocious and inventive than day one, Carrie Brownstein and Corin Tucker's alchemical connection has made Sleater-Kinney one of the most impactful and vital rock acts of their generation. Their self-titled 1995 debut demonstrated a singular vision - the duo's idiosyncratic and interlocking musical language composed of the most dynamic elements of punk, riot grrrl, classic rock fury, and modern indie rock guile. The following year's Call the Doctor brought that mercurial structure into clearer focus, and 1997's Dig Me Out amped the bombast - netting a spot on Rolling Stone's "500 Greatest Albums of All Time." The critical fervor that the band had started amassing was only matched by their ravenous fans, inspired by Sleater-Kinney's propulsive intentionality, intense emotional honesty, galvanized feminism, and explosive live shows. While the band members spent the intervening years on other projects \(including Brownstein's creating and starring in Portlandia\) fans were overjoyed at Sleater-Kinney's 2015 return with the triumphant No Cities To Love - which showed no sign of lost time and found the band yet again near the top of countless year-end lists. THE EXPERIENCE Join us for a screening of a Summer Tour, a poetic documentary about the Deadhead experience: an unconventional family bound together by music, freedom, and the open road. After the screening, we're thrilled to have the Garcia Birthday Band join us for a full set with a liquid light show and handmade posters for sale too! ON SCREEN: Summer Tour 2025. Directed by Mischa Richter. Runtime: 82 minutes. Summer Tour is a poetic documentary that follows Jerry and Annie, a magnetic young couple devoted to the music and community of Dead & Company, as they journey across America for the band's final tour. Blending intimate portraiture with lyrical road imagery, the film captures the essence of the Deadhead experience: an unconventional family bound together by music, freedom, and the open road. At once a love story and a celebration of a uniquely American tradition of wandering, Summer Tour reflects on what it means to seek belonging, adventure, and transcendence in a fleeting moment of cultural history. ON STAGE: Garcia Birthday Band Garcia Birthday Band, based in Portland Oregon, isn't your mother's Grateful Dead cover band. Playing for over 20 years, GBB has evolved into something far deeper than the sum of its parts. The beating heart of the Pacific Northwest's GD community, the band's ever-expanding fanbase is an experience unto themselves. Using the Dead's repertoire as a springboard for limitless potential and improvisation, Garcia Birthday Band are a cornerstone of the modern Grateful Dead universe, and their fans have come to expect the unexpected as the norm. Placing no boundaries on eras of the Dead's career or catalog, and drawing on decades of individual and shared experience, GBB play the music through an auditory kaleidoscope. Composed of some of the most ace players of the Oregon live music community, the band makes every show an act of exploration, both musically and spiritually. United hearts and minds blur the line between the stage and crowd - a carnival of human potential. If you're new to Garcia Birthday Band, their doors are always open, and you'll recognize it as something familiar when you first walk in: home. You may recognize the fellas in GBB from acts such as Nine Days Wonder, Cubensis, Shafty, Turkey Bouillon Mafia, The Campfire Boys, Deadhenge, Shadow of Sound, The Buds of May, The Ike Willis Band, Dead Sessions, and Dark Matter Transfer. events.summary: Written in 1936, this light-hearted comedy has relevance for today in addressing the main theme of finding one’s own way in today’s complex society, while lightly viewing such topics as distrust of government, domestic terrorism and fear of foreign conflicts. “Grandpa” Vanderhof (Robert Lovitz) once worked in the competitive business world. One day, he realized he was unhappy, so he stopped working. Since then, he spends his days catching and raising snakes, watching graduation ceremonies, visiting old friends, and doing whatever else he wants. His daughter Penny (Marilyn Stacey) writes plays simply because a few years ago a typewriter was delivered to the house by accident. His son-in-law Paul Sycamore (Todd Hermanson) spends hours in the basement making illegal fireworks and playing with erector sets. His granddaughter Essie (Bonnie Auguston) sells candy and has been clumsily attempting ballet for over eight years. His grandson-in-law Ed Carmichael (Aiden Brown) plays the xylophone (or tries to) and accidentally distributes Marxist propaganda. Joining this free-for-all are Rheba (Caren Graham), the household cook; her unemployed boyfriend, Donald (Shaun Hennessy); Essie’s opinionated Russian ballet instructor, Mr. Kolenkhov (Mark Schwahn); Olga (Trisha Todd), a Russian Grand Duchess; Gay Wellington (Adrienne Southard), a heavy-drinking actress; Wilbur C. Henderson (Douglas Hout), a forlorn IRS employee; and Mr. De Pinna (Danny Bruno), a deliveryman who arrived 8 years ago and decided to stay. He now helps with the fireworks and dresses in Roman togas to pose for Penny’s portraits. All is somewhat calm until three men from the government (Christopher Sparks, Dan Weiss, and Erik James) visit to investigate Ed’s flyers. In this crazy mix of characters, there is also Alice (Taylor Jean Grady), Penny and Paul’s other daughter and, apparently, the only “normal” family member. She met Tony Kirby (Noah Matthew Rich) at his dad’s Wall Street investment firm, and they’ve fallen in love. Culture shock and fireworks fly when Mr. Kirby (Jeremy Southard) and Mrs. Kirby (Wendy Martel) come to visit. But the message is clear: “Life’s pretty simple if you just relax,” as Grandpa puts it. You Can’t Take It With You is directed by Don Alder. Set design is by Chris Whitten, lighting design is by Demetri Pavlatos, costume design is by Janelle Sutton, prop design is by Allen R. Phillips, the stage manager is Alex Salem, the assistant stage manager is Nat Weinham, and the producer is Steve Knox.

events.summary: SEPTEMBER FLIGHT FEATURING 2 SOLOS BY Don Nigro September 11–27 Fri/Sat 7:30, Sun 2 $38 per person Imago Theatre, 17 SE 8th Avenue imagotheatre.com TICKETS https://onthestage.tickets/show/imago-theatre/6a56bc1797fd36b14c05ee83 Tickets also available at the door. Theatre opens one hour before showtime. All seats $38. The show is for mature audiences. The Dark, performed by Joe Cullen (Salomé, Design for Living) and Cincinnati, performed by Diane Slamp (Geography of a Horse Dreamer, Design for Living). Direction by Jerry Mouawad. THE DARK A man in his thirties grapples with a fundamental question: does he truly exist? This dilemma, first encountered at age four, drives the narrative of this ten-page script. Director Jerry Mouawad calls it "the perfect warm-up for Nigro’s work and his intriguing solos, many of which take place in a theatre." CINCINNATI "It’s hard not to feel that this piece was written specifically for Imago," says Slamp, who portrays a lost professor navigating a world of tragedy, sex, and philosophical diatribes. Her diversions reveal a desperate search for redemption amidst personal disaster. "Cincinnati is multi-layered, blending mythology and realism with an ontological examination of life and being," explains Mouawad. "It’s a gem for an audience seeking a new kind of theatre. Don’t let the heavy themes mislead you; this is a small spectacle with humor and high style. I see it as a consciousness tangling with forces of nature, an uncertain reality, and a triad of personas—real or unreal—in a lecture that pushes the boundaries of endurance.” Production Credits: *Light Design:* Ronnie Rantis Costume Design: Laura Helgeson Sound Design: Myrrh Larsen Note: For Mature Audiences In October, Imago returns with October Flight, featuring more solos by Don Nigro.

Simon reads from The Dolphin Ambassador’s Daughter, feat. music from Sanae Yamada, Barry Walker Unit, and Serafima Doors: September 11, 2026 7:30 PM Online Scheduled Ticket Price: GA: $15.00 Bright Spider Press Presents: Richard B. Simon reads from The Dolphin Ambassador’s Daughter Featuring Musical Performance and Accompaniment by Sanae Yamada, Barry Walker Unit, and Serafima September 11, 12, 13, 2026 in the Pacific Northwest Author, rock journalist, and Frisco Freakout co-founder Richard B. Simon reads from his debut novel The Dolphin Ambassador’s Daughter, a finalist for the PEN/Bellwether Prize for Socially Engaged Fiction, with a little help from his psych rock, cosmic country, and freak folk friends. Richard B. Simon will read from his new novel The Dolphin Ambassador’s Daughter, with musical backing and full sets from Sanae Yamada \(Moon Duo, Vive la Void\), and the Barry Walker Unit \(featuring Ripley Johnson of Wooden Shjips, Moon Duo, and Rose City Band\), and a very special set by Serafima \(Serafima and the Shakedowns\) of new material inspired by the novel. The Dolphin Ambassador’s Daughter is a green fable in the vein of Animal Farm, Watership Down, The Lord of the Rings, and The Odyssey. After a devastating oil spill destroys his homewaters and kills off his entire family, resident orca K’Tangu ShakTii travels to the Great Council of dolphins, whales, walruses, and seals, and demands war to drive the humans from the Ocean. But the Dolphin Ambassador knows that war against the humans would be disastrous, and sends his granddaughter, Zzzwooieee, on a forbidden mission to prevent the war. The novel is about war and peace; ecological destruction, resistance, and resilience; how all living beings respond to injustice and trauma; and how we all might make the world. more just. And it’s sung by a couple of Humpbacks. Along with sets from ambient sound sculptor Sanae Yamada, improvisational psych- country outfit the Barry Walker Unit, and singer-songwriter Serafima, Simon will read selections from the novel with Yamada and then the Barry Walker Unit backing. Serafima will perform a set of songs inspired by the novel. Sanae Yamada is the co-founder of and keyboard player and vocalist in Moon Duo, and has also performed and recorded as Vive La Void. She wrote and performed the musical score for the acclaimed play Is This a Room, about the imprisoned National Security whistleblower Reality Winner. Yamada’s latest album, Room Tone \(Music From Line Time\), is out now on Jean Sandwich Records. events.summary: "Returning to the get down: Goodbye 1969" Legend Zeppelin was never built to recreate a single moment — it was built to live inside the same unpredictability that defined Led Zeppelin on stage. In 1969, no two Zeppelin shows were alike. Songs stretched, shifted, and collided in real time — shaped by the room, the crowd, and the band’s willingness to take risks. That volatility wasn’t a flaw. It was the point. Legend Zeppelin operates the same way. Every performance is a new exchange of energy between band and audience. Tempos change. Sections expand. Improvisations appear and disappear. What happens on stage is never repeated... and never will be. Experience songs like “As Long As I Have You” — a track few bands would dare attempt, before it’s removed from the set permanently. As Legend Zeppelin moves into 1970 next year, the sound, the setlists, and the energy will evolve with it. No resets. No recreations. No going back. Just like the original band, the journey only moves forward. One more night. And then 1969 is gone.
events.title: Legend Zeppelin

events.summary: Surgery always carries some level of risk, and not every unexpected outcome is the result of negligence. However, when a healthcare professional fails to meet the accepted standard of medical care and that failure causes avoidable harm, the situation may amount to Surgical Negligence. Determining the difference often requires a careful review of medical records, expert opinions, and the circumstances surrounding the procedure. Warning signs can include operating on the wrong site, delayed treatment of complications, retained surgical instruments, anesthesia errors, or inadequate post-operative care. It is also important to consider whether the patient was properly informed of the risks before consenting to surgery. Establishing negligence involves proving that the injury was preventable and directly caused by substandard care rather than an unavoidable complication. Because these cases can be medically and legally complex, professional legal guidance is essential. Ciano Carroll Solicitors represents individuals who believe they have suffered avoidable harm due to medical errors and helps them understand whether they may have a valid claim. Their experience in handling complex medical negligence matters enables clients to navigate the legal process with confidence. By working with independent medical experts and thoroughly investigating each case, the firm evaluates whether the required legal standard for negligence has been met. Anyone concerned about the outcome of a surgical procedure should seek advice as early as possible to protect their legal rights. Understanding the distinction between an accepted surgical risk and Surgical Negligence is the first step toward determining whether compensation may be available.
events.title: How can you tell if a surgical complication was actually negligence?

events.summary: The Multnomah Arts Center (MAC) in Portland, Oregon will open two new exhibitions in its Front and Center Galleries this August. tende·r·eprisal // futu·re·prise, a group exhibition of bronze works created by multiple artists through a collaborative process led by elijah jamal asani, will be featured in the Front Gallery. In the Center Gallery, large-scale wood sculptures by Philip A. Robinson Jr. will be paired with functional and sculptural ceramic works by Swapna Mukhopadhyay. Both exhibitions run August 7–September 12, 2026, with a joint reception on Thursday, August 20, from 6 to 8 p.m. elijah jamal asani, a Nigerian-American artist, convened an intergenerational group of regional Black artists to create a collection of contemporary bronze artifacts. Their work was made in response to the historic theft of the Benin Bronzes. “Dating back to the 13th century, artists from the Kingdom of Benin, which is in modern-day southern Nigeria, cast bronze into sacred altar pieces and vessels of ancestral memory,” says asani. “However, in 1897, thousands of these bronze artifacts were looted by British forces.” They have yet to be repatriated. As an act of “selfdetermined restitution,” asani worked with other Black artists to create new bronzes. MAC is honored to exhibit eleven of these sculptures, created by Adriene Cruz, Midnite Seed Abioto, Intisar Abioto, Hanifah Abioto, Vaughn Kimmons, Turiya Raiah, Nyasiah Calixte, Lea Dry, Hannah Dry, Nawens Dry, and elijah jamal asani. Swapna Mukhopadhyay creates functional and sculptural porcelain works, all hand built. “The combination of aesthetics and functionality in handmade folk artifacts has always fascinated me,” she says. “My grandmother made traditional Bengali quilts (kanthas) and wove mats for sitting on the floor (asanas). I now realize how deeply I was influenced by watching her work.” Delicate drawn elements adorn many of her ceramic surfaces, and several recent works incorporate textiles and found objects. Mukhopadhyay describes her process as “improvising around what’s available,” informed by her longtime study of ethnomathematics. A retired PSU professor, she sees mathematics as inherent to creative practice and creative expression as integral to daily life across many cultures. Her ceramic pieces are often small in scale and characterized by what she calls their “putting togetherness.” Philip A. Robinson Jr. is a sculptor and conceptual artist whose work has been exhibited nationally and internationally. Working primarily in wood and metal, Robinson creates large-scale figurative and patterned works that explore memory, structure, and identity. “My practice examines structure as a living system—how materials carry memory, how patterns encode history, and how built environments shape identity,” he explains. “Whether in wood or steel, I am asking how structure holds memory—and how we locate ourselves within it.” The exhibition will include pieces from several bodies of work, including a 42” x 61” sculpture from Welcome In, which examines belonging, and several works from The House of Regina, which honor the legacy of his late mother, Dr. Regina Arnold. Robinson holds a BFA in Studio Art from Skidmore College and an MFA in Sculpture from the Mason Gross School of the Arts at Rutgers University. The Multnomah Arts Center is located at 7688 SW Capitol Hwy, Portland, OR, 97219. It is open Monday – Thursday 9 a.m. to 9:30 p.m., and Friday – Saturday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The galleries are free and open to the public during these hours. Additional Information: The Multnomah Arts Center is a part of Portland Parks & Recreation. MAC offers programs in a wide range of visual, music, movement, theater, and literary arts at an affordable cost to people of all ages. In addition to this vibrant arts education program, MAC runs a community-based visual arts exhibition program, which includes the MAC Front & Center Galleries. MAC also hosts theatre, music and dance performances, and other special events. The Multnomah Arts Center Association (MACA) is an all-volunteer, 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that exists to support equity and access to arts education at MAC. MACA provides scholarships, supports community engagements efforts, and provides specialized arts equipment and facility improvements. Their efforts expand opportunities and enhance the experience of students, instructors, and the community at-large. For more information about MAC or MACA, please call 503.823.2787 or visit www.multnomahartscenter.org

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Last Thursday Artist Reception August 27, 6 to 9pm. Show Dates: August 27 through September 21. Outside City Limits Forget the commute. Turn the car around! Leave civilization behind and delight in the fused-glass landscapes of Linda Gerrard and wander through the threaded tree paintings of Michelle L. Purvis instead. Michelle’s lifelong fascination with trees, mountains, and how they relate to humans strongly influences her art. In this series of framed acrylic paintings on paper, each work is a portrait of a specific tree, dressed in embroidered finery to fit its personality. She made their acquaintance and sketched them from life while she was camping or on vacation. While they may have been created completely in her studio, Linda’s fused-glass landscapes evoke a real sense of natural place. Starting with a base sheet of glass, she builds her images by arranging and kiln-firing layer after layer of colored glass, often leaving lovely textured details on the surface. Linda and Michelle, two long-time members of the gallery, invite you to take in the vistas of meadow, marsh and mountainside, to reach out to stroke the colorful bark of the trees or a heron’s plumage, and to discover what lies just Outside City Limits. Showing in the front windows of Alberta Street Gallery. Alberta Street Gallery is a cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.

events.summary: This September, rediscover the joys of Portland’s oldest arts and entertainment neighborhood with the Ankeny Alley Staycation Street Fair and the Portland Staycation Weekend! Celebrate the artistic history of southwest Old Town and the newly dubbed Pink Light District in carnival style with performances, vendors, and revelry all along the six block stretch from the waterfront to Big Pink! Featuring vendors at the Saturday Market and along Ankeny, roving performances by some of Portland’s best circus, street performance, and musical artists, and Staycation specials at businesses throughout the Pink Light District, this three-day spectacle of food, festivities, and fun caps off with staggered Pink Light Processions - an all-ages community celebration reviving the “pilgrimages of pleasure seekers” of the 1920s with a family friendly twist! Join us on a joyous procession from the SW Waterfront to the Paris Theatre Patio in your favorite pink costume, craft project, or outfit - the bigger the better because you ARE the float for this rose colored revel filled with Portland-style whimsy and weird! Plus, be sure to grab one of our custom directory fliers and build your personal Pink Light itinerary: bring the whole family on a stroll through the Saturday Market, visit Voodoo Donuts, dip in to Dan and Louis for dinner, and treat your tastebuds at Black Cat Custard; or make it a daycation just for the adults with a meal at Mother’s, a drop by Dante’s for a dram, then catch a show at the Can Can and pop in for bite-sized burlesque at Madam Cooper’s Parlor. The choice is yours to mix and match with more than thirty iconic businesses, old and new, to choose from! Check out all of the Pink Light District businesses here: https://www.pinklightpdx.org/explore#business-list What To Expect: The Ankeny Alley Staycation Street Fair kicks off with discounts and specials on food, drink, and more at the neighborhood’s regular events and area businesses on Friday. Then we head into Portland Staycation weekend with two days of vendors, roaming performers, featured Ankeny Alley Stage performances, and the Pink Light Processions - community celebrations down southwest Ankeny filled with music, art, and whimsy! Event Schedule: Friday, 9/11 - All Day - Community art installation, drink, food, and sale specials, and regular events in the Pink Light District - Burnside to Pine and SW 5th to the SW Waterfront - Prices and Age Restrictions Vary Saturday, 9/12 - 11am - 6pm - Vendors and roaming performers - SW Ankeny Street Waterfront to 5th Avenue - FREE, All Ages Saturday, 9/12 - leaving at 3:30pm, 4:00pm, and 4:30pm- Pink Light Processions - Staggered community processions from Saturday Market to Big Pink featuring performance stops, community engagement, music, and roaming performers - SW Ankeny Street Waterfront to 5th Avenue - FREE, All Ages Sunday, 9/13 - 11am - 2pm \- Vendors plus featured circus, busking, and street style performances on the Ankeny Alley Stage - SW Ankeny Street Waterfront to 5th Avenue - FREE, All Ages About Ankeny Alley Association and The Pink Light District: The Ankeny Alley Association is a community-led 501(c)3 business association whose mission is to foster collaboration and support between the businesses and organizations within and surrounding Ankeny Alley. Created to bring together local business owners, the Association quickly grew into a community hub and the caretaking agency for the Ankeny Alley Plaza cultivating neighborhood arts, entertainment, and events in the plaza through support from the neighborhood's commercial and non-profit members. Stretching from West Burnside to Pine Street and from Naito Parkway to 6th Avenue, the Pink Light District brings together artists, businesses, venues, and neighbors to create a cleaner, safer, and more active downtown. Home to beloved landmarks including the Paris Theatre, Kit Kat Club, Voodoo Doughnut, Portland Saturday Market, the Waterfront Cherry Blossoms, and the city's iconic Big Pink tower, the district celebrates everything that makes Portland creative, quirky, and unforgettable. Photo Credits: Promotional design by Myrrh Larsen

In addition, the exhibition offers visions from Portland’s past, from Edward Bennett’s 1932 plan to reenvision Portland in the City Beautiful movement to Skidmore Owings Merrill’s “Delta Dome,” a 40,000-seat stadium in Delta Park, to GGN’s radical re-envisioning of Mt Tabor Park. It is for people and by people, and it cannot be replicated. With TBA, we will show up to experience the moment, the tension, the beauty. events.summary: Founded in 2025 by award-winning classical guitar virtuoso and Artistic Director, Tye Austin, M.M., Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness is a fiscally sponsored nonprofit concert series presenting open-air classical guitar concerts staged in the wilderness of the Pacific Northwest. From August 1 through October 1, Oregon native Tye Austin will perform more than 30 intimate outdoor concerts across 15 of Oregon's most breathtaking state parks—from coastal bluffs to old-growth forests, red rock canyons, thundering waterfalls, vineyards, and ranches. Audiences will experience world-class live music performances through our signature Wilder Sound wireless headphone technology, allowing every guest to enjoy crystal-clear audio while remaining immersed in the beauty of the natural world up to a 1/4 mile radius from the stage. Wilder Frets is more than a concert series. It is a community movement dedicated to making exceptional live music concerts and masterclasses accessible to everyone. Every ticket purchased helps support our growing community initiatives, including: Fret Not Tickets Program, providing complimentary concert tickets to individuals and families facing financial barriers. The Free Frets Initiative, donating free classical guitars, free masterclasses, and mentorship to at-risk from rural, tribal, and urban communities throughout Oregon. Our inaugural season has been made possible through the generosity of our season sponsors and community partners such as Heartbeat Silent Disco, Community Beats, Willamette Valley Music Company, the Maslow Project, and Oregon State Parks who believe that arts, education, conservation, and public access belong together. Whether you're an experienced concertgoer, an outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a meaningful way to spend an evening, Wilder Frets offers an unforgettable experience unlike anything else in the Pacific Northwest. Join us this season and discover why music sounds even more extraordinary in the great outdoors. View complete tour schedule and purchase tickets online only at www.wilderfrets.org/tour
events.title: Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness - Inaugural Concert Season

events.summary: An unflinching documentary portrait of artist, activist, and survivor Logan Lynn, tracing a 30-year career forged at the intersection of queerness, faith, addiction, trauma, and self-reinvention. Structured around the songs from Lynn’s latest record of the same name, the film treats music not as background but as a living character. Beginning in rural Nebraska and Texas inside a fundamentalist Christian world hostile to any type of difference, the film follows Lynn’s early sense of displacement, religious trauma, and abuse, and the ways secrecy and fear shaped both identity and survival. Through intimate interviews with Lynn, and decades of archival footage and home movies, the film charts a restless trajectory: early success, underground acclaim, addiction, public collapse, and the slow, deliberate work of rebuilding a life on one’s own terms. Behind the scenes footage from early music videos, vintage tour clips, and present-day studio conversations collide with moments of humor, tenderness, and brutal honesty. The result is neither a redemption arc nor a nostalgia piece, but a meditation on what it means to outlive the versions of yourself that no longer serve you. Director: Cai Indermaur Year: 2026 Country: United States Runtime: TBD
events.title: The Pain and The Power

events.summary: Written in 1936, this light-hearted comedy has relevance for today in addressing the main theme of finding one’s own way in today’s complex society, while lightly viewing such topics as distrust of government, domestic terrorism and fear of foreign conflicts. “Grandpa” Vanderhof (Robert Lovitz) once worked in the competitive business world. One day, he realized he was unhappy, so he stopped working. Since then, he spends his days catching and raising snakes, watching graduation ceremonies, visiting old friends, and doing whatever else he wants. His daughter Penny (Marilyn Stacey) writes plays simply because a few years ago a typewriter was delivered to the house by accident. His son-in-law Paul Sycamore (Todd Hermanson) spends hours in the basement making illegal fireworks and playing with erector sets. His granddaughter Essie (Bonnie Auguston) sells candy and has been clumsily attempting ballet for over eight years. His grandson-in-law Ed Carmichael (Aiden Brown) plays the xylophone (or tries to) and accidentally distributes Marxist propaganda. Joining this free-for-all are Rheba (Caren Graham), the household cook; her unemployed boyfriend, Donald (Shaun Hennessy); Essie’s opinionated Russian ballet instructor, Mr. Kolenkhov (Mark Schwahn); Olga (Trisha Todd), a Russian Grand Duchess; Gay Wellington (Adrienne Southard), a heavy-drinking actress; Wilbur C. Henderson (Douglas Hout), a forlorn IRS employee; and Mr. De Pinna (Danny Bruno), a deliveryman who arrived 8 years ago and decided to stay. He now helps with the fireworks and dresses in Roman togas to pose for Penny’s portraits. All is somewhat calm until three men from the government (Christopher Sparks, Dan Weiss, and Erik James) visit to investigate Ed’s flyers. In this crazy mix of characters, there is also Alice (Taylor Jean Grady), Penny and Paul’s other daughter and, apparently, the only “normal” family member. She met Tony Kirby (Noah Matthew Rich) at his dad’s Wall Street investment firm, and they’ve fallen in love. Culture shock and fireworks fly when Mr. Kirby (Jeremy Southard) and Mrs. Kirby (Wendy Martel) come to visit. But the message is clear: “Life’s pretty simple if you just relax,” as Grandpa puts it. You Can’t Take It With You is directed by Don Alder. Set design is by Chris Whitten, lighting design is by Demetri Pavlatos, costume design is by Janelle Sutton, prop design is by Allen R. Phillips, the stage manager is Alex Salem, the assistant stage manager is Nat Weinham, and the producer is Steve Knox.
events.title: You Can't Take It With You

events.summary: SEPTEMBER FLIGHT FEATURING 2 SOLOS BY Don Nigro September 11–27 Fri/Sat 7:30, Sun 2 $38 per person Imago Theatre, 17 SE 8th Avenue imagotheatre.com TICKETS https://onthestage.tickets/show/imago-theatre/6a56bc1797fd36b14c05ee83 Tickets also available at the door. Theatre opens one hour before showtime. All seats $38. The show is for mature audiences. The Dark, performed by Joe Cullen (Salomé, Design for Living) and Cincinnati, performed by Diane Slamp (Geography of a Horse Dreamer, Design for Living). Direction by Jerry Mouawad. THE DARK A man in his thirties grapples with a fundamental question: does he truly exist? This dilemma, first encountered at age four, drives the narrative of this ten-page script. Director Jerry Mouawad calls it "the perfect warm-up for Nigro’s work and his intriguing solos, many of which take place in a theatre." CINCINNATI "It’s hard not to feel that this piece was written specifically for Imago," says Slamp, who portrays a lost professor navigating a world of tragedy, sex, and philosophical diatribes. Her diversions reveal a desperate search for redemption amidst personal disaster. "Cincinnati is multi-layered, blending mythology and realism with an ontological examination of life and being," explains Mouawad. "It’s a gem for an audience seeking a new kind of theatre. Don’t let the heavy themes mislead you; this is a small spectacle with humor and high style. I see it as a consciousness tangling with forces of nature, an uncertain reality, and a triad of personas—real or unreal—in a lecture that pushes the boundaries of endurance.” Production Credits: *Light Design:* Ronnie Rantis Costume Design: Laura Helgeson Sound Design: Myrrh Larsen Note: For Mature Audiences In October, Imago returns with October Flight, featuring more solos by Don Nigro.

events.summary: Surgery always carries some level of risk, and not every unexpected outcome is the result of negligence. However, when a healthcare professional fails to meet the accepted standard of medical care and that failure causes avoidable harm, the situation may amount to Surgical Negligence. Determining the difference often requires a careful review of medical records, expert opinions, and the circumstances surrounding the procedure. Warning signs can include operating on the wrong site, delayed treatment of complications, retained surgical instruments, anesthesia errors, or inadequate post-operative care. It is also important to consider whether the patient was properly informed of the risks before consenting to surgery. Establishing negligence involves proving that the injury was preventable and directly caused by substandard care rather than an unavoidable complication. Because these cases can be medically and legally complex, professional legal guidance is essential. Ciano Carroll Solicitors represents individuals who believe they have suffered avoidable harm due to medical errors and helps them understand whether they may have a valid claim. Their experience in handling complex medical negligence matters enables clients to navigate the legal process with confidence. By working with independent medical experts and thoroughly investigating each case, the firm evaluates whether the required legal standard for negligence has been met. Anyone concerned about the outcome of a surgical procedure should seek advice as early as possible to protect their legal rights. Understanding the distinction between an accepted surgical risk and Surgical Negligence is the first step toward determining whether compensation may be available.
events.title: How can you tell if a surgical complication was actually negligence?

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

Get Admission Meet the Instructors: Many Roads Martial Arts Center Jenny Lohr, Owner/Instructor Jenny has been practicing Shaolin Kung Fu and Tai Chi since 2005. As the owner of Many Roads Martial Arts Center, her focus is nurturing a supportive and safe learning environment while challenging everyone to keep growing and improving. Jay Twitchell, Instructor Jay has studied various martial arts systems including boxing, wrestling, judo, karate, taekwondo, aikido, hopkido, kumdo, and muay thai kick boxing since he was 10. In other words, he has been used as a punching bag for over 30 years by masters and lifelong practitioners of these systems. events.summary: Last Thursday Artist Reception August 27, 6 to 9pm. Show Dates: August 27 through September 21. Outside City Limits Forget the commute. Turn the car around! Leave civilization behind and delight in the fused-glass landscapes of Linda Gerrard and wander through the threaded tree paintings of Michelle L. Purvis instead. Michelle’s lifelong fascination with trees, mountains, and how they relate to humans strongly influences her art. In this series of framed acrylic paintings on paper, each work is a portrait of a specific tree, dressed in embroidered finery to fit its personality. She made their acquaintance and sketched them from life while she was camping or on vacation. While they may have been created completely in her studio, Linda’s fused-glass landscapes evoke a real sense of natural place. Starting with a base sheet of glass, she builds her images by arranging and kiln-firing layer after layer of colored glass, often leaving lovely textured details on the surface. Linda and Michelle, two long-time members of the gallery, invite you to take in the vistas of meadow, marsh and mountainside, to reach out to stroke the colorful bark of the trees or a heron’s plumage, and to discover what lies just Outside City Limits. Showing in the front windows of Alberta Street Gallery. Alberta Street Gallery is a cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.

Curated by Alberta Street Gallery member Leslie McMillan, this invitational exhibition features six artists—Larry Holt, Bobby Pedersen, Cindy Caufman, John Hyland, Diane Moskowitz, and Ann Coskey—who harness extreme temperatures to bend raw materials to their vision. events.summary: This September, rediscover the joys of Portland’s oldest arts and entertainment neighborhood with the Ankeny Alley Staycation Street Fair and the Portland Staycation Weekend! Celebrate the artistic history of southwest Old Town and the newly dubbed Pink Light District in carnival style with performances, vendors, and revelry all along the six block stretch from the waterfront to Big Pink! Featuring vendors at the Saturday Market and along Ankeny, roving performances by some of Portland’s best circus, street performance, and musical artists, and Staycation specials at businesses throughout the Pink Light District, this three-day spectacle of food, festivities, and fun caps off with staggered Pink Light Processions - an all-ages community celebration reviving the “pilgrimages of pleasure seekers” of the 1920s with a family friendly twist! Join us on a joyous procession from the SW Waterfront to the Paris Theatre Patio in your favorite pink costume, craft project, or outfit - the bigger the better because you ARE the float for this rose colored revel filled with Portland-style whimsy and weird! Plus, be sure to grab one of our custom directory fliers and build your personal Pink Light itinerary: bring the whole family on a stroll through the Saturday Market, visit Voodoo Donuts, dip in to Dan and Louis for dinner, and treat your tastebuds at Black Cat Custard; or make it a daycation just for the adults with a meal at Mother’s, a drop by Dante’s for a dram, then catch a show at the Can Can and pop in for bite-sized burlesque at Madam Cooper’s Parlor. The choice is yours to mix and match with more than thirty iconic businesses, old and new, to choose from! Check out all of the Pink Light District businesses here: https://www.pinklightpdx.org/explore#business-list What To Expect: The Ankeny Alley Staycation Street Fair kicks off with discounts and specials on food, drink, and more at the neighborhood’s regular events and area businesses on Friday. Then we head into Portland Staycation weekend with two days of vendors, roaming performers, featured Ankeny Alley Stage performances, and the Pink Light Processions - community celebrations down southwest Ankeny filled with music, art, and whimsy! Event Schedule: Friday, 9/11 - All Day - Community art installation, drink, food, and sale specials, and regular events in the Pink Light District - Burnside to Pine and SW 5th to the SW Waterfront - Prices and Age Restrictions Vary Saturday, 9/12 - 11am - 6pm - Vendors and roaming performers - SW Ankeny Street Waterfront to 5th Avenue - FREE, All Ages Saturday, 9/12 - leaving at 3:30pm, 4:00pm, and 4:30pm- Pink Light Processions - Staggered community processions from Saturday Market to Big Pink featuring performance stops, community engagement, music, and roaming performers - SW Ankeny Street Waterfront to 5th Avenue - FREE, All Ages Sunday, 9/13 - 11am - 2pm \- Vendors plus featured circus, busking, and street style performances on the Ankeny Alley Stage - SW Ankeny Street Waterfront to 5th Avenue - FREE, All Ages About Ankeny Alley Association and The Pink Light District: The Ankeny Alley Association is a community-led 501(c)3 business association whose mission is to foster collaboration and support between the businesses and organizations within and surrounding Ankeny Alley. Created to bring together local business owners, the Association quickly grew into a community hub and the caretaking agency for the Ankeny Alley Plaza cultivating neighborhood arts, entertainment, and events in the plaza through support from the neighborhood's commercial and non-profit members. Stretching from West Burnside to Pine Street and from Naito Parkway to 6th Avenue, the Pink Light District brings together artists, businesses, venues, and neighbors to create a cleaner, safer, and more active downtown. Home to beloved landmarks including the Paris Theatre, Kit Kat Club, Voodoo Doughnut, Portland Saturday Market, the Waterfront Cherry Blossoms, and the city's iconic Big Pink tower, the district celebrates everything that makes Portland creative, quirky, and unforgettable. events.summary: Written in 1936, this light-hearted comedy has relevance for today in addressing the main theme of finding one’s own way in today’s complex society, while lightly viewing such topics as distrust of government, domestic terrorism and fear of foreign conflicts. “Grandpa” Vanderhof (Robert Lovitz) once worked in the competitive business world. One day, he realized he was unhappy, so he stopped working. Since then, he spends his days catching and raising snakes, watching graduation ceremonies, visiting old friends, and doing whatever else he wants. His daughter Penny (Marilyn Stacey) writes plays simply because a few years ago a typewriter was delivered to the house by accident. His son-in-law Paul Sycamore (Todd Hermanson) spends hours in the basement making illegal fireworks and playing with erector sets. His granddaughter Essie (Bonnie Auguston) sells candy and has been clumsily attempting ballet for over eight years. His grandson-in-law Ed Carmichael (Aiden Brown) plays the xylophone (or tries to) and accidentally distributes Marxist propaganda. Joining this free-for-all are Rheba (Caren Graham), the household cook; her unemployed boyfriend, Donald (Shaun Hennessy); Essie’s opinionated Russian ballet instructor, Mr. Kolenkhov (Mark Schwahn); Olga (Trisha Todd), a Russian Grand Duchess; Gay Wellington (Adrienne Southard), a heavy-drinking actress; Wilbur C. Henderson (Douglas Hout), a forlorn IRS employee; and Mr. De Pinna (Danny Bruno), a deliveryman who arrived 8 years ago and decided to stay. He now helps with the fireworks and dresses in Roman togas to pose for Penny’s portraits. All is somewhat calm until three men from the government (Christopher Sparks, Dan Weiss, and Erik James) visit to investigate Ed’s flyers. In this crazy mix of characters, there is also Alice (Taylor Jean Grady), Penny and Paul’s other daughter and, apparently, the only “normal” family member. She met Tony Kirby (Noah Matthew Rich) at his dad’s Wall Street investment firm, and they’ve fallen in love. Culture shock and fireworks fly when Mr. Kirby (Jeremy Southard) and Mrs. Kirby (Wendy Martel) come to visit. But the message is clear: “Life’s pretty simple if you just relax,” as Grandpa puts it. You Can’t Take It With You is directed by Don Alder. Set design is by Chris Whitten, lighting design is by Demetri Pavlatos, costume design is by Janelle Sutton, prop design is by Allen R. Phillips, the stage manager is Alex Salem, the assistant stage manager is Nat Weinham, and the producer is Steve Knox.

events.summary: SEPTEMBER FLIGHT FEATURING 2 SOLOS BY Don Nigro September 11–27 Fri/Sat 7:30, Sun 2 $38 per person Imago Theatre, 17 SE 8th Avenue imagotheatre.com TICKETS https://onthestage.tickets/show/imago-theatre/6a56bc1797fd36b14c05ee83 Tickets also available at the door. Theatre opens one hour before showtime. All seats $38. The show is for mature audiences. The Dark, performed by Joe Cullen (Salomé, Design for Living) and Cincinnati, performed by Diane Slamp (Geography of a Horse Dreamer, Design for Living). Direction by Jerry Mouawad. THE DARK A man in his thirties grapples with a fundamental question: does he truly exist? This dilemma, first encountered at age four, drives the narrative of this ten-page script. Director Jerry Mouawad calls it "the perfect warm-up for Nigro’s work and his intriguing solos, many of which take place in a theatre." CINCINNATI "It’s hard not to feel that this piece was written specifically for Imago," says Slamp, who portrays a lost professor navigating a world of tragedy, sex, and philosophical diatribes. Her diversions reveal a desperate search for redemption amidst personal disaster. "Cincinnati is multi-layered, blending mythology and realism with an ontological examination of life and being," explains Mouawad. "It’s a gem for an audience seeking a new kind of theatre. Don’t let the heavy themes mislead you; this is a small spectacle with humor and high style. I see it as a consciousness tangling with forces of nature, an uncertain reality, and a triad of personas—real or unreal—in a lecture that pushes the boundaries of endurance.” Production Credits: *Light Design:* Ronnie Rantis Costume Design: Laura Helgeson Sound Design: Myrrh Larsen Note: For Mature Audiences In October, Imago returns with October Flight, featuring more solos by Don Nigro.

events.summary: Founded in 2025 by award-winning classical guitar virtuoso and Artistic Director, Tye Austin, M.M., Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness is a fiscally sponsored nonprofit concert series presenting open-air classical guitar concerts staged in the wilderness of the Pacific Northwest. From August 1 through October 1, Oregon native Tye Austin will perform more than 30 intimate outdoor concerts across 15 of Oregon's most breathtaking state parks—from coastal bluffs to old-growth forests, red rock canyons, thundering waterfalls, vineyards, and ranches. Audiences will experience world-class live music performances through our signature Wilder Sound wireless headphone technology, allowing every guest to enjoy crystal-clear audio while remaining immersed in the beauty of the natural world up to a 1/4 mile radius from the stage. Wilder Frets is more than a concert series. It is a community movement dedicated to making exceptional live music concerts and masterclasses accessible to everyone. Every ticket purchased helps support our growing community initiatives, including: Fret Not Tickets Program, providing complimentary concert tickets to individuals and families facing financial barriers. The Free Frets Initiative, donating free classical guitars, free masterclasses, and mentorship to at-risk from rural, tribal, and urban communities throughout Oregon. Our inaugural season has been made possible through the generosity of our season sponsors and community partners such as Heartbeat Silent Disco, Community Beats, Willamette Valley Music Company, the Maslow Project, and Oregon State Parks who believe that arts, education, conservation, and public access belong together. Whether you're an experienced concertgoer, an outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a meaningful way to spend an evening, Wilder Frets offers an unforgettable experience unlike anything else in the Pacific Northwest. Join us this season and discover why music sounds even more extraordinary in the great outdoors. View complete tour schedule and purchase tickets online only at www.wilderfrets.org/tour
events.title: Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness - Inaugural Concert Season

THE EXPERIENCE We welcome back local filmmaker and producer Barbara Bernstein and her film Chasing Chimeras: The Lure of Deceptive Climate Solutions, which tells the stories of people living in the crosshairs of the fossil fuel industry's self-serving climate solutions, including renewable diesel, hydrogen, renewable natural gas, biofuels, carbon capture and storage, and carbon offsets. Following the film, Barbara will lead a discussion. ON SCREEN: Chasing Chimeras: The Lure of Deceptive Climate Solutions 2025. Directed by Barbara Bernstein. Runtime: 55 minutes. As we confront the existential crisis of climate chaos, there are two paths we can take. We can make dramatic changes that meaningfully reduce carbon emissions, or we can accept the fossil fuel industry's self-serving climate solutions-renewable diesel, hydrogen, renewable natural gas, biofuels, carbon capture and storage, and carbon offsets. Chasing Chimeras: The Lure of Deceptive Climate Solutions tells stories of people living in the crosshairs of these proposals, working to expose the dangers that these projects pose to their lives, homes, communities, and the planet. In contrast to fossil fuel industry solutions, the documentary examines the need to implement verified and trusted renewable energy sources \(wind, solar, and geothermal\), energy conservation, and nature-based carbon capture and storage solutions that take advantage of natural carbon sinks such as old growth forests and wetlands. ON STAGE: Barbara Bernstein \(Director\) - ProducerBarbara Bernsteinis a musician, composer, performance artist, radio producer and filmmaker. Besides her recent documentaries "Chasing Chimeras" and "Once a Braided River," her award-winning radio documentaries, internationally broadcast on public radio stations, include two pieces about the struggle to stop the Pacific Northwest from becoming a fossil fuel export hub: Holding the Thin Green Line and Sacrifice Zones; Sculpted By Fire \(the role of fire in shaping western forests and sustaining healthy forest ecosystems\); Salmonlands \(the cultural significance of diminishing salmon runs in the Northwest\) and Rivers That Were \(the industrialization of the Colorado and Columbia Rivers\). She is currently working on a new documentary about liberating the culverted creeks that flow under Portland's Industrial sacrifice zone along the Willamette River. events.summary: When it comes to storytelling, very few pop groups have done it as well as Squeeze. But even the group’s songwriting mainstays Chris Difford and Glenn Tilbrook would be hard pushed to devise a plot twist like the one that has resulted in Trixies, their first album in eight years. Because, if truth be told, the band who have given us sky-high classics such as ‘Up The Junction’, ‘Tempted’, ‘Cool For Cats’, ‘Another Nail In My Heart’ and ‘Labelled With Love’ weren’t planning another album. And that was ok. They’d scaled the highs of pop stardom; they’d disbanded and reconvened; fallen out and made up. Along the way, they got to bear witness to the effect their songbook has had on generations of fans – their compositions covered by artists as disparate as Erykah Badu, Tricky, Patti Austin, The Shins, Joe Cocker, The Lathums and Questlove & Robert Glasper. Their songs even pop up from time to time on Desert Island Discs, most recently when comedian Bob Mortimer revealed that he had already requested that the title track of their 1993 album Some Fantastic Place be played at his funeral
events.title: Squeeze - Tried, Tested and Trixies With Special Guest Adam Ant and Haircut 100
